description: NOTICE OF INTENT to Sole Source SOLICITATION NUMBER: 75N98026Q01114 TITLE: MRI 16 Channel Preamplifier Interface Boxes CLASSIFICATION CODE: 6525 � Imaging Equipment and Supplies: Medical, Dental, Veterinary NAICS CODE: 423450 � Medical, Dental and Hospital Equipment and Supplies Merchant Wholesalers RESPONSE DATE: September 14, 2026 PRIMARY POINT OF CONTACT: Robin Knightly, Contracting Officer Research & Development, Division A National Institutes of Health, Office of the Director robin.knightly@nih.gov PURSUANT TO FAR Subpart 5.2 � Synopses of Proposed Contract Actions, THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE OF A PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION. THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NON-COMPETITIVE NOTICE OF INENT TO AWARD A CONTRACT OR PURCHASE ORDER WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL OR OPEN COMPETITION (INCLUDING BRAND-NAME). DESCRIPTION: On behalf of the Neurophysiology Imaging Facility (NIF), the National Institutes of Health, Office of the Director, intends to solicit on a sole-source basis by a request for quotation to Rogue Research, Inc. to acquire two (2) 16-Channel Preamp Interface Boxes for Takashima Marmoset Coil on or around September 15, 2026 with an award issued on or around September 15, 2026. The purpose of this acquisition is to acquire two (2) 16-Channel Preamp Interface Boxes for Takashima Marmoset Coil for an existing Government-owned Takashima Marmoset Coil. NORTH AMERICAN INDUSTRY CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (NAICS) CODE and SET ASIDE STATUS The intended procurement is classified under NAICS code 423450 with a Size Standard of 500 employees. This acquisition is NOT set aside for small businesses but rather is a sole-source acquisition to Rogue Research, Inc. REGULATORY AUTHORITY The resultant contract will include all applicable provisions and clauses of the Federal Acquisition Requlation (FAR) in effect through the Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 dated March 13, 2026. STATUTORY AUTHORITY This acquisition is conducted under the authority of the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 12� Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. For purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, Contracting officers may solicit from one source IF the contracting officer documents that only one source is available and the basis for their decision. BACKGROUND, PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES OF REQUIREMENT NIF operates a dedicated 7T MRI system for structural, functional, and diffusion imaging in anesthetized and awake marmosets. The three Takashima 16-channel receive arrays, acquired five years ago, have consistently produced high signal-to-noise ratio and accelerated imaging performance essential for advanced neuroimaging studies. Each receive array requires a compatible 16-channel preamplifier interface. The current inventory of two aging preamplifiers has demonstrated susceptibility to channel failure, and extended repair times have exposed vulnerability in system redundancy. Given the high utilization of the 7T MRI system by multiple laboratories, lack of available preamplifiers directly impacts scanner availability and research productivity. The objective is to establish sufficient hardware redundancy by acquiring two additional 16-channel preamplifier interface boxes to ensure continuous scanner readiness, preserve data quality standards, and sustain ongoing and future marmoset neuroimaging programs at NIF. Delivery or Deliverables Please see the attached Purchase Description for further details. CLOSING STATEMENT THIS NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD ON A SOLE-SOURCE BASIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be considered by the agency. The information received will normally be considered solely for the purposes of determining whether to proceed on a non-competitive basis or to conduct a competitive procurement. Responses to this notice shall contain sufficient information to establish the interested parties' bona-fide capabilities for fulfilling the requirement and include: unit price, list price, shipping and handling costs, the delivery period after contract award, the prompt payment discount terms, the F.O.B. Point (Destination or Origin), the Dun & Bradstreet Number (DUNS), the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), and the certification of business size. All offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) www.sam.gov.www.sam.gov.� All responses must be received by Monday, September 14, 2026 at 9:00 a.m., Eastern Standard Time, and reference number 75N98026Q01114. Responses may be submitted electronically to Robin Knightly, Contracting Officer, at Robin.Knightly@nih.gov. Fax responses will not be accepted. Extensions to the deadline will not be granted. Please contact Robin Knightly, Contracting Officer, at Robin.Knightly@nih.gov or (301) 827-5302 with any questions.

title: Neubau Feuerwehrhaus der Stadt Rietberg - Türen, Zargen, Feuerschutztüren
description: Im Rahmen dieser Leistung sind sämtliche Innen-, Stahl- und Feuerschutztüren einschließlich der zugehörigen Stahlzargen zu liefern und betriebsfertig zu montieren. Zum Leistungsumfang gehören die Erstellung und Abstimmung einer vollständigen Türliste, die Lieferung und Montage von Stahlzargen für Mauerwerks- und Trockenbauwände sowie die Ausführung von Innentüren mit hochbeanspruchbaren HPL-beschichteten Vollspan-Türblättern für Büro-, Aufenthalts- und Funktionsbereiche. Insgesamt werden über 25 Innentüranlagen in unterschiedlichen Abmessungen sowie mehrere ein- und zweiflügelige Stahltüren ausgeführt. Darüber hinaus sind fünf T30-Feuerschutztüren mit Stahlzargen und HPL-Oberflächen sowie weitere feuerhemmende und rauchdichte Stahl-Feuerschutztüren als zugelassene Komplettsysteme zu liefern und einzubauen. Die Türen werden mit hochwertigen Edelstahlbeschlägen, Obentürschließern, Schallschutz-, Rauchschutz- und Panikfunktionen entsprechend den jeweiligen Anforderungen ausgestattet. Ergänzend sind diverse Sonderausstattungen wie Feucht- und Nassraumausführungen, absenkbare Bodendichtungen, Glasausschnitte, WC-Beschilderungen und Türschließsysteme vorzusehen. Bestandteil der Ausschreibung sind außerdem die jährliche Inspektion und Wartung aller Feuerschutztüren während der vierjährigen Gewährleistungszeit einschließlich Dokumentation und Prüfprotokollen.

description: The proposed Framework Contract for the period 1 June 2027 to 31 May 2031 will ensure the continued provision of security guard services required to protect Mission personnel, facilities and assets, while enabling the uninterrupted implementation of the Mission's activities throughout the contract period in accordance with the EEAS Minimum Security Operating Standards and the EEAS Field Security Policy. The selected contractor will provide security guarding services for the EUAM HQ, Mission facilities and field presence on a 24/7 basis, including, but not limited to, the following services: a) Physical protection of Mission personnel, premises, equipment and other assets, including parking areas where applicable, as well as the accommodation of international Mission Members, in accordance with the highest applicable safety and security standards. b) Security services at Mission facilities, including access control during office hours, vehicle and visitor screening, internal and external patrols outside office hours, incident reporting, and monitoring of CCTV systems, intrusion alarms and fire detection systems. c) Security Response Teams (SRTs) responsible for monitoring designated patrol areas and responding to alarms or emergency calls at Mission offices and/or the accommodation of Mission Members.

title: Neubau Feuerwehrhaus der Stadt Rietberg - Fliesenarbeiten (Verlegung)
description: Die Ausschreibung umfasst ausschließlich die Verlegung und Verarbeitung der Fliesenbeläge einschließlich aller notwendigen Verlege- und Abdichtungsmaterialien. Die keramischen Wand-, Boden-, Mosaik- und Sockelfliesen werden bauseits geliefert und stehen dem Auftragnehmer zur Verarbeitung zur Verfügung. Der Auftragnehmer hat die gelieferten Fliesen innerhalb des Gebäudes an die jeweiligen Einbauorte zu vertragen, fachgerecht zu verlegen und sämtliche Verpackungsmaterialien zu entsorgen. Im Rahmen dieser Leistung sind sämtliche Abdichtungs-, Verlege- und Anschlussarbeiten für keramische Wand- und Bodenbeläge im Feuerwehrgebäude auszuführen. Die Arbeiten umfassen die Herstellung von Verbundabdichtungen gemäß DIN 18534 in Dusch-, Sanitär-, Waschhallen- und Nassbereichen, die Verlegung von Wand- und Bodenfliesen einschließlich Mosaikbelägen, Hohlkehlsockeln, Sockelfliesen sowie die Ausbildung aller erforderlichen Anschluss-, Bewegungs- und Silikonfugen. Ergänzend sind Untergrundvorbereitungen, Spachtel- und Ausgleichsarbeiten, Gerüststellungen, Ausschnitte für Installationen, Abdichtungen an Bodenabläufen und Entwässerungsrinnen sowie verschiedene Naturstein- und Bauplattenarbeiten auszuführen. Insgesamt werden rund 195 m² Wandfliesen, 694 m² Bodenfliesen, 25 m² Mosaikbeläge in Duschbereichen sowie umfangreiche Sockel-, Hohlkehlsockel-, Natursteinfensterbank- und Abdichtungsarbeiten ausgeführt. Die Leistungen beinhalten sämtliche Kleber-, Fugen- und Dichtstoffe sowie alle Nebenarbeiten zur vollständigen und gebrauchsfertigen Herstellung der Fliesenflächen.

title: Collaborative Interface and Prototyping Design Tool
description: This bid solicitation 1000439295/A cancels and supersedes previous bid solicitation number 1000439295 dated September 17, 2024 with a closing of October 16, 2024 at 02:00 PM EDT. The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) intends to enter into a contract with a single contractor to provide 40 user licenses for a Software as a Service ( Saas) Subscription based Licenses for a cloud-based interface design and prototyping tool to support the creation, modification, and collaboration of internal and external CRA digital content, including static and interactive designs for intranet, secure portal, and Canada.ca pages. While the CRA currently uses various software design tools that are adequate for prototyping, these tools do not allow seamless collaboration among project team members. As a result, designs must often be exported into shareable formats such as PowerPoint or PDF for review by team members who do not have access to the design software. This process is time-consuming and inefficient, requiring designers to maintain multiple versions of the same file and increasing the risk that feedback provided on alternate versions may not be incorporated into the final design. The existence of multiple versions in different formats also creates potential version control issues. The CRA is therefore seeking a design and prototyping solution that enables project team members to be assigned view, comment, and edit roles, allowing them to provide feedback directly within design files without requiring individual tool licenses. This will improve sharing, collaboration, efficiency, and version control. This requirement also includes options to to acquire the additional quantities of user licenses for a Software as a Service ( Saas) Subscription based Licenses described at Annex B (see Table 3). The period of any resulting contract is a firm one-year plus the irrevocable option to extend the term of the Contract by up to 5 additional 1-year periods. A bid must comply with all requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory evaluation criteria to be declared responsive. The responsive bid with the lowest evaluated price will then be evaluated in accordance with the Proof of Proposal (POP) testing. Proposal documents and supporting information may be submitted in either English or French. The CRA reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Questions must be directed in writing to the contracting authority via email: magued.elyas@cra-arc.gc.ca Bid Submissions: Bids must be submitted by using the Connect service provided by the Canada Post Corporation. When responding, the proposal MUST be delivered to: Canada Revenue Agency Bid Receiving Unit BRUg@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids will not be accepted if emailed directly to this email address. This email address must be used to request that CRA open a Connect conversation, as detailed in Standard Instructions 2003. Bidders must not use their own licensing agreement for Connect to initiate a Connect conversation with CRA. This bid solicitation 1000439295/A cancels and supersedes previous bid solicitation number 1000439295 dated September 17, 2024 with a closing of October 16, 2024 at 02:00 PM EDT. The main changes in the revised solicitation 1000439295/A are found at: • Appendix 1 - Mandatory Criteria: Two mandatory criterion were removed. Previously M.6.3 & M7; • Appendix 2 - Financial Proposal: The number of firm licenses required was reduced from 80 to 40 consisting of 30 Designer Licenses and 10 partner Licenses; • Annex A- Statement of Requirements: The accessibility requirements changed to use the most recent version and a new category of licenses was added. Any Bidder who submitted a proposal in response to the original solicitation 1000439295 and who wishes to bid on this revised solicitation 1000439295/A must submit an entirely new proposal. By virtue of submitting an entirely new proposal, the bidder affirms that the new proposal supersedes the previous proposal submitted by the bidder. Reciprocal Procurement - Limited Supplier Eligibility Only Canadian Suppliers and Suppliers of an applicable trading partner, as defined in the Reciprocal Procurement Declaration of Part 5 Certifications and Additional Information, are eligible for this solicitation. Bids submitted by Suppliers of a non-trading partner will be rejected. Promoting Accessibility The Accessible Canada Act (the Act) received Royal Assent on June 21, 2019, and came into force on July 11, 2019, with the goal of ensuring the full and equal participation of all persons, especially persons with disabilities, in society. This is to be achieved through the progressive realization of a Canada without barriers, on or before January 1, 2040, particularly by the identification, removal and prevention of barriers in federal jurisdiction in the following priority areas: • employment; • the built environment (buildings and public spaces); • information and communication technologies; • communication, other than information and communication technologies; • the procurement of goods, services and facilities; • the design and delivery of programs and services; and • transportation. The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) is fully committed to the Act’s goal of making Canada barrier-free by January 1, 2040. Following consultations with persons with disabilities, their caregivers, and CRA employees with disabilities concerning the accessibility barriers they have encountered with the CRA’s service offerings, the CRA published its first-ever Accessibility Plan. The plan outlines concrete actions that the CRA will take to identify, remove and prevent accessibility barriers across its programs and services over the next three years. In keeping with the CRA’s Accessibility Plan, and in order to comply with the Act, we are taking steps to procure accessible goods and services in support of the delivery of CRA programs and services. For example, the CRA has adopted the accessibility requirements for information and communication technology (ICT) products and services as outlined in the Harmonised European Standard EN 301 549 v3.2.1 (2021-03). Compliance with this standard must be demonstrated as part of all applicable CRA ICT solicitations and resulting contracts. The CRA continues to explore ways to ensure all other goods and services procured are inclusive by design and accessible by default. As this initiative is intended to take place progressively, suppliers should anticipate that, over time, the accessibility requirements in the CRA’s procurement contracts will evolve and may become more demanding. Accessibility questions or concerns? The CRA invites suppliers to identify any accessibility concerns with this solicitation document or any of the associated requirements. Please address your concerns to the contracting authority identified in this RFP.

title: Indoor Firing Range Rental – Pacific Region Conservation and Protection (C&P)
description: 1. Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) An ACAN is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 2. Title Indoor Firing Range Rental – Pacific Region Conservation and Protection (C&P) 3. Definition of Requirements The Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) has a requirement for the services a suitable indoor firing range facility to support firearms training, qualification, and operational readiness activities for Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) Pacific Region Conservation and Protection (C&P) personnel. DFO requests the Abbotsford Fish and Game Club to provide access to an indoor firing range facility suitable for law enforcement training purposes. The Facility must support simultaneous use by multiple Officers and accommodate standard firearms training activities. The Contractor must, but not limited, to the following: A) Facility Access • Provide scheduled access to the indoor firing range for C&P personnel; • Ensure the Facility is available for bookings as coordinated with the Technical Authority; • Provide safe entry and exit procedures for all authorized personnel. B) Range Operations • Maintain the Facility in safe, clean, and operational condition; • Ensure all shooting lanes, target systems, and safety equipment are functional during scheduled use; • Provide range safety controls consistent with recognized safety standards. C) Environmental Systems • Operate and maintain an air filtration and ventilation system designed to move airflow from the firing line toward the target area; • Ensure that smoke, gases, and particulate matter from firearms discharge are effectively removed from the shooting area to maintain safe air quality. If other potential suppliers submit a statement of capabilities during the 15 calendar days posting period that meet the requirements set out in the ACAN, DFO/CCG will proceed to a full-tendering process on whether the government's electronic tendering service or through traditional means, in order to award the Contract. If no other supplier submits on or before the closing date, a statement of capabilities meeting the requirements set out in the ACAN, a Contract will be awarded to the pre-selected supplier. 4. Criteria for Assessment of the Statement of Capabilities (minimum essential requirements) Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements: • Operate a legally compliant indoor firing range facility; • Demonstrate experience in providing range services for law enforcement, military, or equivalent clients • Maintain appropriate insurance and certifications required for operation of an indoor firearms range; • Ensure staff are trained in range safety and emergency procedures. a) Shooting Lanes Minimum lane length of 25 meters; Minimum of 10 shooting lanes; Ability to accommodate up to 10 concurrent shooters. b) Firearms Compatibility The range must be rated and approved for: 9mm pistol ammunition (full metal jacket and hollow point); 12-gauge shotgun slug ammunition. c) Environmental Controls Air filtration and ventilation system must: Direct airflow toward the target end; Rapidly clear smoke and discharge from the firing area; Maintain air quality appropriate for prolonged indoor shooting activities. d) Lighting Conditions The Facility must provide adjustable lighting conditions, including low-light shooting capability. e) Temperature Control The Facility must be temperature controlled and capable of maintaining comfortable indoor conditions during cooler weather. f) Amenities The Facility must provide access to washroom facilities for all authorized users. 5. Trade Agreements See the description of the Posting. 6. Security Requirements This contract does not contain any security requirements. 7. Justification for the Pre-Identified Supplier The pre-identified supplier is the only supplier that we are aware of who offers a product which meets all the Minimum Essential Requirements listed above. 8. Exception to the Government Contracts Regulations The following exception(s) to the Government Contracts Regulations is (are) invoked for this procurement under subsection 6(d) – “only one person is capable of performing the work.” 9. Contract Period The Contract period will be from award to August 31, 2030 inclusive. 10. Estimated Cost The estimated value of the Contract is 216,525.00 $ CAD (excluding applicable taxes). 11. Name and Address of the Proposed Contractor Abbotsford Fish and Game Club 4161 Lakemount Road Abbotsford, BC V2T 6Z 12. Suppliers’ right to submit a statement of capabilities Suppliers who consider themselves fully qualified and available to provide the services/goods described herein, may submit a Statement of Capabilities in writing, by e-mail, to the contact person identified in this Notice on or before the closing date and time of this Notice. The Statement of Capabilities must clearly demonstrate how the supplier meets the advertised requirements. 13. Closing Date The closing date for a submission of a Statement of Capabilities is September 14, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. EDT. 14. Requests for information and submission of statements of capabilities Request for information and statements of capabilities must be sent before the date and time indicated in Article 13, to: Contract Authority Manon Paulin, Senior Contracting Officer Procurement and Material Management Fisheries and Oceans Canada Telephone : 438-468-3247 Email : DFO.Tenders-Soumissions.MPO@dfo-mpo.gc.ca

title: A.1 Application/Software Architect – Java, Level 3
description: The senior application software architect will be required to design and implement architectural solution for the suite of application systems supported by PBDID . Additionally, the resource will be required to provide advice and guidance regarding optimal architectural designs and software solutions to PBDID staff , its client and DTSS senior management as required. Duties and deliverables may include but not be limited to the following: • Translate business requirements into an architected solution; • Propose best approach to configure solution optimizing for performance and cost efficiencies; • Design solution architecture to support optimal solution delivery and integration • Design solution architecture to optimize solution performance and build to scale • Clearly articulate design considerations including defining solution risk/benefit analysis • Produce documentation such as solution design documents, options analysis, configuration standards; • Lead solution design sessions, architect and document solutions; • Recommend industry best practices to technology and business stakeholders; • Provide knowledge transfer to PBDID team members through documentation and information sessions including hands-on assistance to developers, business analysts, user interface designers, and other relevant team members; and • Provide updates/status reporting to project team management as required. • Present proposed solution architecture for approval to Departmental Management and Executive Committees as required

description: This engagement consists of three components. Components 1 and 2 constitute a single requirement and will be awarded under one contract. title: Mänttä-Vilppulan kaupungin suurkeittiö-, kylmälaitteiden huolto-, korjauspalvelut ja vuototarkastukset
description: Mänttä-Vilppulan kaupungin suurkeittiö-, kylmälaitteiden huolto-, korjauspalvelut ja vuototarkastukset Mänttä-Vilppulan kaupungin tilapalvelut hakee puitesopimuskumppaneita suurkeittiölaitteiden, sekä kylmälaitteiden huoltoon, korjaukseen ja vuototarkastuksiin. Koneiden ja laitteiden huoltojen ja korjausten toimittajaksi valitaan kolme (3) hinnaltaan edullisinta toimittajaa. Huolto- ja korjauspalveluiden tilaukset tehdään etusijajärjestyksessä. Huolto tilataan etusijajärjestyksessä 1. toimittajalta. Mikäli 1. toimittaja ei pysty palvelua toimittamaan, ostetaan palvelu 2. toimittajalta ja mikäli tämäkään toimittaja ei pysty palvelua toimittamaan, tilataan palvelu 3. toimittajalta jne. Määräaikaishuollot tehdään valitun toimijan kanssa yhteistyössä sovittujen kokonaisuuksien jaerillisen huolto-ohjeen sekä laiteluettelon mukaan 1-2 x vuodessa. Määräaikaishuollot merkitään tehdyksi huoltokirjaan sekä laitteeseen kiinnitetään tarra tai erillinen huoltotagi, mistä näkee kunkin laitteen huoltopäivämäärän. Huollon yhteydessä havaitut puutteet sekä laitteiden uusimistarpeet raportoidaan tilaajalle määräaikaishuollonyhteydessä. Mahdolliset järjestelmätäytöt ja huolto-ohjeesta poikkeavat työt laskutetaan tuntiperusteisesti. Tämän sopimuksen piiriin eivät kuulu takuuaikaiset huolto- ja korjaustyöt, jotka tekee kyseisenlaitteen toimittaja.,

Salient Characteristics are defined as containing the same active ingredient(s), and same concentrations that must be met for a chemical to be considered brand name or equal. For the CLARKSBURG Louis A Johnson VA MEDICAL CENTER. 1 Medical CTR DRIVE, Clarksburg, WV 26301. All responsible sources may submit a capabilities statement and answer the subcontracting questions listed below. At minimum the below response must include the following. All responses must include the following information or will not be considered. Please respond to this Sources Sought Notice 36C24526Q0812 with your: 1. Business name (including Unique Entity ID (SAM.gov) 2. Business type, socio-economic status (e.g., Veteran-Owned, Woman-Owned, Disadvantaged Small Business, 8(a), etc.), and 3. Person of contact (including telephone number & email address). 4. Capability statement and summary of previous experience providing these types of services for the Veterans Health Administration or other similar facilities. 5. Available contract vehicles (GSA FSS, etc.) for use by Department of VA (include applicable NAICS) 6. Brief Summary of categories of services that your company can/cannot provide. 7. Certification(s) / Licenses for meeting the local requirements to provide these services at the DC VAMC (if applicable) 8. Confirmation that your organization has the capability & expertise to meet the performance requirements while complying with applicable limitations in subcontracting by responding to the questions below with your response: a. Do you intend to self-perform this effort? b. If you are located outside the immediate area, how will you self-perform? c. Or do you intend to subcontract work under this contract? d. If you intend to subcontract work under this contract, how will you ensure compliance with the limitations on subcontracting? Please include certifications or knowledge that demonstrate competency. Electrical License Must be able have the ability for Installing or interfacing with a UPS especially a three phase 80 kVA system Certifications working with Liebert/Vertiv UPS systems requires familiarity with their installation, electrical interface, battery system, control wiring, commissioning practice, and safety requirements. LOC out Tag out procedures, OSHA 10/30 Training Certifications NFPA 70E certification. Commissioning of Liebert unit Must Respond with all information by September 14th, 2026, at 10:00 AM ET. Send all responses to Bill Pratt, Billie.Pratt@va.gov STATEMENT OF WORK SCOPE OF WORK PROJECT DATA: a) TITLE: Server Room UPS Rental b) BUILDING/FACILITY: Bldg. 1 LAJVAMC 2. GENERAL SCOPE This project covers the delivery, installation, and start-up, of a rental 80 KVA UPS. Contractor will verify the existing connected load to an existing Liebert UPS: Model 37BP080XWXCBNR Serial # 3T00005193 Perform all necessary demolition and site preparations to install a temporary UPS of the same size and capacity as existing. Due to space limitations, it is anticipated that the existing Liebert UPS referenced above will require full disassembly and removal prior to the placement and connection of a temporary UPS of comparable size and capacity. The Contractor shall be responsible for all labor, materials, equipment, and tools necessary to complete the delivery, demolition of existing, installation of temporary and start-up, maintenance (if required), and removal of the rental equipment to include disassembly at the end of the rental period. The Contractor shall clean the work area daily and secure all tools and materials for patient and staff safety. 3. GENERAL CONDITIONS AND DEFINITIONS COR:� Contracting Officer s Representative. A VA employee of the Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center Facilities Management Service officially assigned to act as Project Manager and Inspector. The COR shall be the primary point of contact on all matters concerning the contract work. Coordination:� All administrative and logistical requirements regarding the project must be exclusively coordinated with the assigned COR. No other person has authority to direct or approve changes to contract work unless specifically authorized. Provide (Rental):� For the purpose of this scope, the term Provide means to deliver, install, and make available for use fully functional rental UPS system(s) and associated battery cabinet per manufacturer s instructions and SOW requirements. Remove (Rental Return):� At the conclusion of the rental period, all equipment will be disconnected and prepared for return shipment to the vendor. The vendor will coordinate pickup and removal with the COR. The contractor shall remove all debris resulting from delivery, installation, and start-up immediately upon completion of the activity. The work site will be left clean and orderly at all times. All activities shall correspond to this Scope of Work. Any discrepancy identified between this SOW and actual site conditions shall be promptly brought to the attention of the VA COR before continuation. 4. DETAILED REQUIREMENTS Equipment to be Provided and Installed: UPS Systems (Qty 1): Size, model capacity to be field verified by vendor based on existing connected load. Reference 80 kVA Liebert UPS as basis for comparison. Services Included: Delivery of all rental equipment to the loading dock at Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center, 1 Medical Center Drive, Clarksburg, WV 26301. Start-up services by a qualified Sure Power Engineer (does not include on-site commissioning or load testing). Return (outbound) shipping at the end of the rental period. All equipment shall remain the property of the rental vendor and be maintained in accordance with manufacturer s specifications during the rental period. Maintenance and Service Schedule: The Contractor shall provide a detailed maintenance and service schedule for the rental equipment to the VA Contracting Officer s Representative (COR) prior to or upon equipment delivery. This schedule shall include all planned maintenance, inspections, and required servicing for the duration of the rental period. Any updates or changes to the maintenance schedule must be promptly communicated to the COR. Documentation of all performed maintenance and service activities shall be submitted to the VA for tracking and recordkeeping purposes. Customer Responsibilities: Provide a safe, accessible location for equipment installation at Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center. Installation and all required external cabling to be done by the VA or as otherwise coordinated. Notify contractor of any required schedule changes or access issues at least 72 hours in advance. Site and Safety Requirements: Contractor is responsible for all activities related to the safe delivery, set-up, energizing, and de-energizing of the rental units. All packaging, dunnage, and debris from delivery, start-up, or removal must be promptly cleaned up and removed off government property daily. VA dumpsters may not be used. Performance Verification: After start-up, the Contractor shall demonstrate in-service that the UPS units and battery cabinets are functioning as intended, in coordination with VA technical staff. Any technical troubleshooting or warranty service during the rental shall be promptly performed by the Contractor or their designee. At the conclusion, the Contractor shall participate in the power-down and removal of both the UPS and battery cabinet and coordinate all return logistics. 5. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS A. Contractor shall comply with all applicable Federal, State, and Local requirements regarding safety and health, including but not limited to OSHA statutes and regulations. The contractor is solely responsible for determining applicable requirements and ensuring a safe and healthful worksite. B. The Contractor shall take precautions to protect Government property at all times. C. The Contractor shall observe all facility fire, safety, and security requirements, including protection

title: Training Analysis Evaluation Product Request for Proposal (8A Set-Aside)

description: Dear Prospective Quoter: Subject: Request for Quotations number 19AJ2026Q0019 Enclosed is a Request for Quotations (RFQ) for Inspection and Repair of Fuel Tanks at the U.S. Embassy Baku, Azerbaijan. If you would like to submit quotation, follow the instructions in Section 3 of the solicitation, complete the required portions of the attached document, and submit it to the address shown on the Standard Form 1449 that follows this letter. The U.S. Government intends to award a contract/purchase order to the responsible company submitting an acceptable offer at the lowest price. We intend to award a contract/purchase order based on initial quotations, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies in the competitive range if there is a need to do so. The Embassy intends to conduct a pre-quotation conference at the site, The pre-proposal conference will be held on September 2, 2026, at 10:00 am (local time) at the US Baku (111 Azadliq ave.). Prospective offerors/quoters should contact Anar Rzayev by September 1, 2026, 15:00 (local time) for additional information or to arrange entry to the building. Quotations are due by September 14, 2026, 18:00 local time. No quotations will be accepted after this time. Proposals must be in English and incomplete proposals will not be accepted. Your quotation must be submitted electronically to BAKUBIDBOX@STATE.GOV It is important to make sure the submission is made in specific size and format; in MS-Word 2007/2010 or MS-Excel 2007/2010 or Adobe Acrobat (pdf) file format. The file size must not exceed 30MB. If the file size should exceed the 30MB, the submission must be made in separate files and attached to separate emails with less than 30MB each. In order for a quotation to be considered, you must also complete and submit the following: 1. SF-1449 2. Section I, Pricing 3. Section 5 Representations and Certifications 4. Additional information as required in Section 3 5. Proof of SAM Registration (please see attached instruction file for registration) Offerors shall be registered in the SAM (System for Award Management) database at https://www.sam.gov prior to submittal of their offer/proposal as prescribed under FAR 4.1102. Failure to be registered at time of proposal submission may deem the offeror�s proposal to be considered non-responsible and no further consideration will be given. Therefore, offerors are highly encouraged to register immediately if they are interested in submitting a response to this requirement.

title: NCR Transportation
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) ONLY. The government seeks to procure a non-personnel services contract to provide ground transportation for family members of U.S. Army Soldiers in and around the National Capital Region (NCR) area. The NCR encompasses Washington, DC; Montgomery and Prince George's Counties in Maryland; Arlington, Fairfax, Loudoun, and Prince William Counties in Virginia; and the incorporated cities of Alexandria, Falls Church, Fairfax, and Manassas in Virginia. The contractor must be registered with the Defense Travel Management Office (DTMO Approved Carrier Listing (ACL) to be considered for the award. A small business set-aside will be considered, provided two (2) or more qualified small businesses respond to this sources sought notice with information sufficient to support a set-aside. Be advised that the U.S. Government will not be able to set aside this requirement if two (2) or more small businesses do not respond with information to support the set-aside. We encourage all small businesses, in all socioeconomic categories (including, 8(a) Business Development Program, Small Disadvantage Business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned Small Business concerns), to identify their capabilities in meeting the requirement at a fair market price. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ)/Invitation for Bid (IFB)/Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. Government is not seeking quotes, bids or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this sources sought notice. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ or IFB or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Government-wide Point of Entry. It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor the Government-wide Point of Entry for additional information pertaining to this requirement. The anticipated NAICS code(s) is/are: 485999-All Other Transit and Ground Passenger Transportation Attached is the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) for details. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice shall be e-mailed to the Contract Specialist, Zachery E Reynolds, at zachery.e.reynolds.civ@army.mil and the Contracting Officer, Deborah R Davis-Maxwell, at deborah.r.davis-maxwell.civ@army.mil, no later than 14 September 2026 at 10:00a.m. EST (Fort Knox local time). Limitations on subcontracting and nonmanufacturer rule do not apply to small business set-asides for contracts at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT). It does apply to 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, EDWOSB, and WOSB set asides regardless of the dollar value of the award. Small business contractors awarded contracts above the SAT are required to comply with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting when utilizing subcontractors. The penalty for non-compliance is the greater of (A) $500K or (B) the dollar amount expended, in excess of permitted levels. See FAR 52.219-14 - Limitations on Subcontracting for Small Business. In response to this sources sought, please provide: Name of the firm, point of contact, phone number, email address, UEI number, CAGE code, a statement regarding small business status (including small business type(s)/certifications(s) such as SDB, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.) and the corresponding NAICS code. Identify whether your firm is interested in competing for this requirement as a prime contractor or not. Identify subcontracting, joint ventures or teaming arrangement that will be pursued, if any. Information in sufficient detail regarding previous experience (indicate whether as a prime contractor or subcontractor) on similar requirements (include size, scope, complexity, timeframe, government or commercial), pertinent certifications, etc., that will facilitate making a capability determination. The information must clearly explain how your firm can satisfy the requirements as outlined in the PWS. General statements of interest will not be used as a capability determination. Information to help determine if the requirement is commercially available, including pricing information, basis for the pricing information (e.g., market pricing, catalog pricing), delivery schedules, customary terms and conditions, warranties, etc. Identify how the Army can best structure these contract requirements to facilitate competition by and among small business concerns. Identify any condition or action that may be having the effect of unnecessarily restricting competition with respect to this acquisition. Please contact the MICC Advocate for Competition, Scott Kukes, at scott.d.kukes.civ@army.mil or 520-944-7373, if you believe that this action is unreasonably restricting competition. Include the subject of the acquisition, this announcement, and the MICC POC information from the notice. Provide the specific aspects that unreasonably restrict competition and the rationale for such conclusion.

title: Court Reporting, Certified Summarized or Verbatim Transcription
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for information and planning purposes (market research) pursuant to FAR Part 10. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Quotation (RFQ), nor does it guarantee a future solicitation. The Government is seeking capability statements from qualified Small Business concerns. Although this requirement is primarily planned as a 100% Small Business set-aside, expressions of interest from other socioeconomic categories (e.g., 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone) will be evaluated to establish the optimal procurement strategy. Scope of Work & Task Requirements: The requirement shall include the following tasks Task 1 � The service provider shall provide court reporter services at hearings. Task 2 � The service provider shall provide verbatim legal transcription of all audio files. Task 3 � The service provider shall ensure all transcription work is conducted within the United States. Task 4 -- The service provider shall not include names of witnesses or interviewees on any external documents. Task 5 � The service provider shall identify speakers throughout the documents. Task 6- The service provider shall provide an initial TRANSCRIPT via electronic copy (.pdf) of each hearing to the Virginia Air National Guard Legal Office for authentication no later than 30 calendar days of the completion of the hearing. Task 7 - After authentication, the service provider shall provide the Virginia Air National Guard Legal Office with one final hard copy (paper) and one final electronic copy (.pdf), within 14 calendar days. Task 8 - The service provider shall ensure transcripts are maintained in strict confidence and free from unauthorized disclosure. Task 9 - The service provider shall turn over physical audio files after each call to the COR. Interested sources must submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to fulfill the operational requirements outlined in this notice. Submissions must address the following elements: Company Profile and Administrative Information: Provide the company's full legal business name, physical address, point of contact details (name, email, phone number), CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) registered in SAM.gov. Business Size and Socioeconomic Status: Clearly identify business size and all socioeconomic certifications under NAICS code 561492 (e.g., Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business [SDVOSB], Woman-Owned Small Business [WOSB], 8(a) Program Participant, or HUBZone). Technical Capability and Personnel Qualifications: Describe your firm's core qualifications, including experience providing certified court reporters for live military/legal hearings, verbatim legal transcription proficiency, quality control processes, and capacity to consistently meet the 30-day draft and 14-day final delivery schedules.

title: J061--SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE - RENTAL OF UPS - Uninterruptible Power Supply FOR PHONE ROOM LOUIS A JOHNSON VA MEDICAL CENTER 36C24526Q0812
description: Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration, Network Contracting Office 5, is issuing this Notice of Sources Sought for a contractor for delivery, installation, and start-up, of a rental 80 KVA UPS. For the CLARKSBURG Louis A Johnson VA MEDICAL CENTER. 1 Medical CTR DRIVE, Clarksburg, WV 26301. All responsible sources may submit a capabilities statement and answer the subcontracting questions listed below. At minimum the below response must include the following. All responses must include the following information or will not be considered. Please respond to this Sources Sought Notice 36C24526Q0812 with your: 1. Business name (including Unique Entity ID (SAM.gov) 2. Business type, socio-economic status (e.g., Veteran-Owned, Woman-Owned, Disadvantaged Small Business, 8(a), etc.), and 3. Person of contact (including telephone number & email address). 4. Capability statement and summary of previous experience providing these types of services for the Veterans Health Administration or other similar facilities. 5. Available contract vehicles (GSA FSS, etc.) for use by Department of VA (include applicable NAICS) 6. Brief Summary of categories of services that your company can/cannot provide. 7. Certification(s) / Licenses for meeting the local requirements to provide these services at the DC VAMC (if applicable) 8. Confirmation that your organization has the capability & expertise to meet the performance requirements while complying with applicable limitations in subcontracting by responding to the questions below with your response: a. Do you intend to self-perform this effort? b. If you are located outside the immediate area, how will you self-perform? c. Or do you intend to subcontract work under this contract? d. If you intend to subcontract work under this contract, how will you ensure compliance with the limitations on subcontracting? Please include certifications or knowledge that demonstrate competency. Electrical License Must be able have the ability for Installing or interfacing with a UPS especially a three phase 80 kVA system Certifications working with Liebert/Vertiv UPS systems requires familiarity with their installation, electrical interface, battery system, control wiring, commissioning practice, and safety requirements. LOC out Tag out procedures, OSHA 10/30 Training Certifications NFPA 70E certification. Commissioning of Liebert unit Must Respond with all information by September 14th, 2026, at 10:00 AM ET. Send all responses to Bill Pratt, Billie.Pratt@va.gov STATEMENT OF WORK SCOPE OF WORK PROJECT DATA: a) TITLE: Server Room UPS Rental b) BUILDING/FACILITY: Bldg. 1 LAJVAMC 2. GENERAL SCOPE This project covers the delivery, installation, and start-up, of a rental 80 KVA UPS. Contractor will verify the existing connected load to an existing Liebert UPS: Model 37BP080XWXCBNR Serial # 3T00005193 Perform all necessary demolition and site preparations to install a temporary UPS of the same size and capacity as existing. Due to space limitations, it is anticipated that the existing Liebert UPS referenced above will require full disassembly and removal prior to the placement and connection of a temporary UPS of comparable size and capacity. The Contractor shall be responsible for all labor, materials, equipment, and tools necessary to complete the delivery, demolition of existing, installation of temporary and start-up, maintenance (if required), and removal of the rental equipment to include disassembly at the end of the rental period. The Contractor shall clean the work area daily and secure all tools and materials for patient and staff safety. 3. GENERAL CONDITIONS AND DEFINITIONS COR:� Contracting Officer s Representative. A VA employee of the Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center Facilities Management Service officially assigned to act as Project Manager and Inspector. The COR shall be the primary point of contact on all matters concerning the contract work. Coordination:� All administrative and logistical requirements regarding the project must be exclusively coordinated with the assigned COR. No other person has authority to direct or approve changes to contract work unless specifically authorized. Provide (Rental):� For the purpose of this scope, the term Provide means to deliver, install, and make available for use fully functional rental UPS system(s) and associated battery cabinet per manufacturer s instructions and SOW requirements. Remove (Rental Return):� At the conclusion of the rental period, all equipment will be disconnected and prepared for return shipment to the vendor. The vendor will coordinate pickup and removal with the COR. The contractor shall remove all debris resulting from delivery, installation, and start-up immediately upon completion of the activity. The work site will be left clean and orderly at all times. All activities shall correspond to this Scope of Work. Any discrepancy identified between this SOW and actual site conditions shall be promptly brought to the attention of the VA COR before continuation. 4. DETAILED REQUIREMENTS Equipment to be Provided and Installed: UPS Systems (Qty 1): Size, model capacity to be field verified by vendor based on existing connected load. Reference 80 kVA Liebert UPS as basis for comparison. Services Included: Delivery of all rental equipment to the loading dock at Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center, 1 Medical Center Drive, Clarksburg, WV 26301. Start-up services by a qualified Sure Power Engineer (does not include on-site commissioning or load testing). Return (outbound) shipping at the end of the rental period. All equipment shall remain the property of the rental vendor and be maintained in accordance with manufacturer s specifications during the rental period. Maintenance and Service Schedule: The Contractor shall provide a detailed maintenance and service schedule for the rental equipment to the VA Contracting Officer s Representative (COR) prior to or upon equipment delivery. This schedule shall include all planned maintenance, inspections, and required servicing for the duration of the rental period. Any updates or changes to the maintenance schedule must be promptly communicated to the COR. Documentation of all performed maintenance and service activities shall be submitted to the VA for tracking and recordkeeping purposes. Customer Responsibilities: Provide a safe, accessible location for equipment installation at Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center. Installation and all required external cabling to be done by the VA or as otherwise coordinated. Notify contractor of any required schedule changes or access issues at least 72 hours in advance. Site and Safety Requirements: Contractor is responsible for all activities related to the safe delivery, set-up, energizing, and de-energizing of the rental units. All packaging, dunnage, and debris from delivery, start-up, or removal must be promptly cleaned up and removed off government property daily. VA dumpsters may not be used. Performance Verification: After start-up, the Contractor shall demonstrate in-service that the UPS units and battery cabinets are functioning as intended, in coordination with VA technical staff. Any technical troubleshooting or warranty service during the rental shall be promptly performed by the Contractor or their designee. At the conclusion, the Contractor shall participate in the power-down and removal of both the UPS and battery cabinet and coordinate all return logistics. 5. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS A. Contractor shall comply with all applicable Federal, State, and Local requirements regarding safety and health, including but not limited to OSHA statutes and regulations. The contractor is solely responsible for determining applicable requirements and ensuring a safe and healthful worksite. B. The Contractor shall take precautions to protect Government property at all times. C. The Contractor shall observe all facility fire, safety, and security requirements, including protection

title: Semiconductor Process Residual Gas Analyzer
description: SOLICITATION 1333ND26QNB640573 Semiconductor Process Residual Gas Analyzer This is a solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Subpart 12.2, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested, and a separate written document will not be issued. This solicitation is a Request for Quotation (RFQ). The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 334516 � Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing with a Small Business size standard of 1,000 Employees. This requirement will be a Full and Open Competition. The Chemical Process and Nuclear Measurements Group is seeking a semiconductor-grade Process Residual Gas Analyzer (RGA) for use on flow systems, including an ALD reactor, as part of a CHIPS R&D Metrology program. This program focuses on developing digital twin technology for semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The flow systems, equipped with in situ and inline sensors, are used to acquire process data on thin film growth characterization. The RGA will serve as an online process diagnostic. The RGA must be compatible with low-volatility organometallic and metal halide precursors and process gases. The data and models generated by this project will lead to improvements in process optimization and control, ultimately resulting in cost savings for the US semiconductor industry.

title: Z2DA--589A7-23-306 Renovate Bldg. 5 & 5B for Mental Health FY27 NRM
description: Project # 589A7-23-306 Renovate 5 & 5B for Mental Health The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 15, has a requirement for Renovate 5 & 5B for Mental Health, project number 589A7-23-306, located at the U.S Department of Veterans Affairs, Robert J. Dole VA Medical Center 5500 E Kellogg Dr, Wichita, KS 67218 The following narrative is intended to provide an overview of the scope of work for the proposed project. Period of Performance 210 calendar days after Notice to Proceed (NTP) Scope of Work Contractor shall perform construction and renovation of the existing space in Building 5 &/or 5B at the Robert J. Dole VA Medical Center campus. This project will prepare approximately 1,100 SF of existing space in building 5 and/or 5B for use as a same day access mental health clinic in adherence to VHA directive 1231(2) & VHA Handbook 1160.1. This project shall be executed in a manner, following the sequence defined in the design narrative, to maintain continuous operations of adjacent VA clinical functions and medical center functionality throughout construction. All construction work shall be performed in full compliance with the complete set of bidding documents, including all contract drawings, specifications, and design narratives associated with this solicitation necessary to convert the existing space into four exam rooms, a combined waiting/reception area, a relocated police office, and associated support spaces. The general contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, tools, and equipment necessary to execute the required scope of work. Construction will consist of, but is not limited to, the following: Selective demolition of existing interior partitions, ceilings, finishes, and elements required for new clinic layout. Installation of new interior finishes including flooring, wall finishes, ceilings, trim, and casework. Implementation of therapeutic design features, including calm color schemes, anchored artwork, secure hardware, and achieving a minimum STC-45 acoustic rating for exam room partitions. Installation of new wall-mounted lavatories in each exam room. Routing new domestic hot and cold water from adjacent restrooms and trenching new water lines across the corridor to existing tin-in points. Rebalancing and modifying HVAC systems; reusing the existing rooftop AHU serving the building; relocating or adding diffusers/grilles; installing ligature-resistant diffusers in exam rooms Providing new electrical receptacles, data outlets, and circuits to support clinical functions Installing LED lighting including secured, ligature-resistant fixtures in exam rooms; relocating or supplementing lighting in general spaces; adding occupancy sensors. Removal of existing sprinklers, providing temporary upright sprinkler coverage during construction, and installing new sprinklers to meet NFPA 13 standards Site preparation for installation of Government furnished equipment, including structural supports, utility connections, and required interfaces. Hazardous materials abatement, including asbestos remediation in areas identified during construction; asbestos containing materials are expected in some work areas and must be removed or handled per applicable VA, EPA, OSHA, and state/local regulations. All other items as described in the contract documents. This construction work is located in an occupied, operational clinical facility and must be performed in a manner that allows medical care services to continue uninterrupted throughout construction, This requires carefully phased construction, strict adherence to ICRA, infection control, noise/vibration limits, and daily coordination with the VA COR and end users. Construction may also include the abatement of any asbestos as identified on the provided drawings. The construction of this project will take place in a very busy occupied building and is to be completed to allow medical care functions to be maintained uninterrupted throughout construction necessitating carefully phased construction and coordination with VA COR/users, including strict adherence to ICRA requirements. The estimated project cost range to complete this work is Between $500,000 and $1,000,000. Pursuant to 38 USC 8127(d) and in accordance with Public Law 109-461, the Veterans Benefits, Health Care and Information Technology Act of 2006, this construction project will be solicited as a Total set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). The North American Industry Classification Code (NAICS) for this procurement is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with a small business size standard of $45.0 million. Contract Type: Firm Fixed. The duration of the project is estimated to be 210 calendar days from Notice to Proceed. This completion period includes final inspection and cleanup of the premises. Award will be made utilizing Highest technically rated with a fair and reasonable price approach in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 15. Proposal submission instructions will be included in the solicitation package. The government plans to award without discussions. The offeror is responsible to monitor and download any amendments from the Contract Opportunities (https:// sam.gov) website, which may be issued to this solicitation. In accordance with FAR 52.204-7, Required SAM, and in accordance with Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 802.101, prospective contractors must be registered in SAM and in the Veteran Small Business Certification (sba.gov) databases under the applicable NAICS. Firms may obtain SAM information at http://www.sam.gov and Veteran Small Business Certification (sba.gov) information at https://veterans.certify.sba.gov The solicitation package with project specifications and drawings should be available for download on or about September 15, 2026 and the proposal due date will be on or about October 15, 2026. An organized site visit will be scheduled and specific date and time will be made available at time of solicitation issuance. Only one site visit will be scheduled and interested offerors are highly encouraged to attend. No hard copies of the solicitation or drawings will be provided; and telephone requests or questions will NOT be accepted. Please email requests or questions to Jennifer.Hill@va.gov and ensure that the subject line reads "Renovate 5 & 5B for Mental Health, Project Number 589A7-23-306; Solicitation Number: 36C25526R0171

Rebalancing and modifying HVAC systems; reusing the existing rooftop AHU serving the building; relocating or adding diffusers/grilles; installing ligature-resistant diffusers in exam rooms Providing new electrical receptacles, data outlets, and circuits to support clinical functions Installing LED lighting including secured, ligature-resistant fixtures in exam rooms; relocating or supplementing lighting in general spaces; adding occupancy sensors. Removal of existing sprinklers, providing temporary upright sprinkler coverage during construction, and installing new sprinklers to meet NFPA 13 standards Site preparation for installation of Government furnished equipment, including structural supports, utility connections, and required interfaces. Hazardous materials abatement, including asbestos remediation in areas identified during construction; asbestos containing materials are expected in some work areas and must be removed or handled per applicable VA, EPA, OSHA, and state/local regulations. All other items as described in the contract documents. This construction work is located in an occupied, operational clinical facility and must be performed in a manner that allows medical care services to continue uninterrupted throughout construction, This requires carefully phased construction, strict adherence to ICRA, infection control, noise/vibration limits, and daily coordination with the VA COR and end users. Construction may also include the abatement of any asbestos as identified on the provided drawings. The construction of this project will take place in a very busy occupied building and is to be completed to allow medical care functions to be maintained uninterrupted throughout construction necessitating carefully phased construction and coordination with VA COR/users, including strict adherence to ICRA requirements. title: MTS Assured Maintenance Plan (AMP)
description: Intent to Sole Source The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC/PZIBA) intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to MTS Systems Corporation, 14000 Technology Drive, Eden Prairie, MN 55344. This contract is for the maintenance, support and repair of proprietary hardware and software configurations of MTS equipment for the Air Force Institute of Technology at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB). Solicitation Number: FA860126Q0125 Classification Code: � NAICS Code: 334519 � Product Service Code (PSC): J066 Extensive market research was conducted to identify potential sources. Techniques included, but were not limited to, a GSA Advantage review, Internet market research, a review of similar procurements at WPAFB, input from Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), and a Sources Sought notice. This research confirmed that MTS Systems Corporation is the only source capable of meeting the Government�s minimum requirements as outlined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The WPAFB Air Force Institute of Technology (AFIT) is already equipped with MTS systems proprietary equipment. To ensure performance, all maintenance services must be from MTS Systems Corporation. Extensive market research confirmed that no other manufacturer can meet this requirement. Therefore, MTS Systems Corporation is the only source capable of providing proprietary services that satisfy the specific requirement of the PWS. Furthermore, AFIT also maintains a preventive maintenance plan for its existing MTS Systems equipment. MTS Systems Corporation offers an extended warranty on their propriety equipment, that will ensure the equipment will be available to support AFIT students. This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." A Justification and Approval for other than full and open competition has been prepared in accordance with RFO 6.104-1, citing the proprietary nature of the required equipment and services. Submission Instructions and Points of Contact: Interested parties who believe they can satisfy the requirements must provide a capability statement with clear and convincing evidence of their ability to do so. The statement must demonstrate the vendor's capability to provide the MTS Assured Maintenance Plan (AMP) plan that is 100% compatible with the proprietary hardware and software, maintenance and meets all requirements in the PWS. A simple statement of capability is not sufficient. All responses, questions, and capability statements shall be submitted via email to the following points of contact no later than Monday, 14 September, 2026, at 11:00 AM Eastern Time. Contract Specialist: Brian Algeo, brian.algeo.1@us.af.mil Contracting Officer: Candice Snow, candice.snow@us.af.mil All correspondence sent via email must contain the subject line: "FA8601-26-Q-0125, MTS Assured Maintenance Plan (AMP)." Be advised that emails without this exact subject line or with prohibited attachments (.zip, .exe) may be blocked by network filters. Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC): Per RDFARS 252.204-7021, this acquisition requires CMMC Level 1 (Federal Contract Information only). Offerors must have a current CMMC Level 1 (or higher) self-assessment recorded in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) at the time of award. Waivers, grace periods, and Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms) are not permitted. Buy American Act and Trade Agreements: This acquisition is subject to the Buy American Act and applicable trade agreements as implemented in the RFO and RDFARS. Offerors shall identify the country of origin for the offered end product and any qualifying components in their Reps and Certs. Domestic or qualifying/designated-country end products are required unless an authorized exception applies. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals or quotes. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. This system will replace a legacy homegrown database that is difficult to update and query. The new software will enable real-time monitoring of SRM locations, track temperature excursions, and fulfill the audit requirements of NIST�s quality systems. NIST Materials Measurement Laboratory (MML) has identified Freezerworks Base Edition as the only freezer inventory software that can meet NIST�s requirements. Freezerworks has been in continuous use at the NIST Hollings Marine Laboratory (HML) for their specimen bank since 2010. To maintain uniform inventory control across different NIST locations and minimize potential operational problems, MML must utilize the same software foundation. Using the same software platform across NIST facilities ensures that data structures, metadata fields, and reporting protocols remain consistent. This standardization is critical for the management of SRM inventory that is distributed across multiple locations. Freezerworks also utilizes a proprietary 4D database engine. Dataworks Development, Inc. is the sole author and provider of this architecture, and they are the only entity capable of providing the "Customer Care Program" renewals required for technical support, security patches, and database diagnostics. Further, Dataworks Development Inc. only sells Freezerworks Base Edition software directly to its customers and does not use authorized resellers. Therefore, this is a sole source purchase that the Government must make directly from Dataworks Development, Inc. General No solicitation package will be issued. title: Germany – Accumulators, primary cells and primary batteries – Batteriespeicher BESS II Harrislee
description: Gegenstand des vorliegenden Projektes ist die Errichtung und der Betrieb eines netzgekoppelten Stand-Alone-Batteriespeichersystems (BESS) mit einer elektrischen Anschlussleistung von 70 MW sowie einer nutzbaren Speicherkapazität von 140 MWh auf dem Betriebsgelände des Kunden. Das Speichersystem soll über einen Mittelspannungstransformator an das kundeneigene 60 kV-Mittelspannungsnetz angebunden werden und dient der Teilnahme am Arbitragehandel. Der Aufstellungsort des Batteriespeichers befindet sich auf einer grünen Wiese, dessen im Besitz der STADTWERKE FLENSBURG GMBH (SWFL) liegt. Die Ausführung des Systems ist als containerisierte bzw. modulare Speicherlösung vorgesehen, bestehend aus Batteriesystemen, Wechselrichtereinheiten, Transformatorentechnik, Schutz- und Leittechnik sowie den erforderlichen Nebenanlagen. Die Speicherkapazität soll zur Teilnahme am Energiehandel eingesetzt werden. Vorgesehen ist insbesondere die Vermarktung von Flexibilitäten über kurzfristige Strommärkte, um Erlöse aus Price Spreads und marktbedingten Arbitragepotenzialen zu generieren. Darüber hinaus soll das Batteriespeichersystem zur Bereitstellung von Sekundärregelleistung (aFRR) eingesetzt werden und somit zusätzliche Erlöse aus der Teilnahme am Regelenergiemarkt erzielen. Durch den marktorientierter Mehrfachnutzung wird eine wirtschaftlich optimierte Betriebsweise des Speichersystems angestrebt.

title: Ireland – Electrical engineering installation works – TII522 Electrical Renewals Works (Low Voltage) IMPQQ
description: TII intends to enter into Multi Party Framework Agreement for Luas Electrical Renewals and Upgrade Works (Low Voltage) for the Luas Light Rail System. This IMPQQ competition aims to identify and shortlist highly qualified electrical contractors with proven electrical expertise and experience in Low Voltage (LV) electrical systems for light rail or heavy rail infrastructure, specifically in the design, installation, testing, commissioning, and compliance of railway electrical systems at LV level. This framework, when established, will be available to TII to draw down from it on a CallOff Contract basis, (PW-CF2 and PW-CF4). The Applicant must demonstrate a strong track record of delivering complex electrical works in live operational rail environments, ensuring safety, quality, reliability, and full regulatory compliance. The Applicant must demonstrate their experience in the design, installation, testing, commissioning of safetycritical electrical systems in live railway environments and compliance of various railway electrical LV systems. Applicants must demonstrate their experience working in live railway environment and must be capable of acting as the Project Supervisor for the Design Process (PSDP) and the Project Supervisor for the Construction Stage (PSCS) in accordance with Irish health and safety legislation. TII are inviting expressions of interest from interested parties to be selected to tender with a view to entering into the Contract. Applicants are referred to the Information Memorandum and Prequalification Questionnaire (IMPQQ) which provides additional information in relation to the competition. Provided that there is a sufficient number of suitable Applicants, TII intends to invite the number of Applicants (as indicated in this IMPQQ) to tender. Prior to shortlisting any Applicant, TII reserves the right to seek verification of any declarations made in the response to the ESPD/IMPQQ.

buyer: UNITED STATES AGENCY FOR GLOBAL MEDIA, BBG
title: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for USAGM Remote Monitoring Services
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for a contract to provide Remote Monitoring Services as described in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The U.S. Agency for Global Media (USAGM) operates international broadcasting services utilizing shortwave (HF) and medium wave (MW) transmission facilities worldwide. To ensure broadcast effectiveness, signal quality, and transmission reliability, USAGM requires contractor support to conduct remote monitoring, signal analysis, propagation assessments, and technical reporting. The objective of this requirement is to obtain remote monitoring support for USAGM shortwave and medium wave broadcasts using USAGM Remote Monitoring Systems (RMS) and contractor-provided monitoring equipment.

title: Type 6 Fire Engines
description: The U. S. Forest Service (USFS) is soliciting a proposal from qualified vendors for thirty-three (33) Type 6 fire engines, body only configuration, to be installed on Government-furnished 4X4 cab and chassis. Scope includes chassis modifications and preparation, installation of the body, fire pump, 300-gallon water tank, warning lights, required graphics package, and all components necessary to deliver a complete operational unit. Apparatus must meet Forest Service national standard specifications, including compliance with NFPA 1900 unless otherwise specified. Proposal shall include delivery of each unit and on-site familiarization training. Vendors shall demonstrate their capability to produce apparatus meeting the requirements of the USFS, summarized in executive form.

description: The Bureau of Medicine and Surgery (BUMED) Medical Readiness (N10D) directorate requires professional support services to oversee force health, deployability, suitability screening, Family Readiness, and disability evaluation processes. The Contractor shall provide policy analysis, data engineering, training development, process improvement, and administrative support across the following functional portfolios: Family Readiness & Specialized Care; Accessions & Retentions; Disability & Limited Duty; Force Health & Individual Medical Readiness. title: 535TRS M4 TRAINER WEAPONS
description: The 502d Contracting Squadron, Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland (JBSA-Lackland), TX intends to solicit and award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price purchase order to Laser Shot, Inc. under the authority of RFO 6.103-1(a) (10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1)). This requirement is for three hundred and fifty (350) M4 Trainer Weapons for the 535th Training Squadron at JBSA-Lackland, TX. Through market research, the Laser Shot M4 Trainer Weapons are determined to be essential to the Government's requirements to maintain absolute instructional continuity and direct compatibility with the existing training inventory, technical manuals, and established Basic Military Training (BMT) curriculum. Laser Shot, Inc. holds the exclusive proprietary manufacturing and design rights for this M4 Trainer Weapon (acquired from Olympic Arms, Inc.), does not utilize authorized resellers or distributors, and is the sole manufacturer of these devices. No other product can meet the training squadron safety and instructional requirements without unacceptable training inconsistencies, duplication of cost, and schedule delays. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 332994 (Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing), with a small business size standard of 1,000 employees. This NAICS code is selected because the M4 Trainer Weapons are structurally inert replica firearms manufactured utilizing actual firearm fabrication processes, tooling, and materials to prevent live-fire conversion. If an interested party believes this NAICS code is incorrect, please provide your recommended NAICS code with a supporting rationale in your response. This NOTICE OF INTENT is not a Solicitation or a Request for Quote. It is a Government notification of the intent to proceed with a Sole-Source acquisition. However, interested parties who believe they can fulfill this requirement may submit a capability statement and past performance narrative. Submissions must clearly demonstrate the capability to provide inert M4 training weapons that possess the standard 10-part field-strip mechanical disassembly realism and a certified, unrestricted, arms-room-free ATF-exempt training status. All capability statements must be submitted via email in response to this notice.

title: Aqualab VSA Vapor Sorption Analyzer
description: The USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) on behalf of USDA Agricultural Research Service intends to award a firm-fixed price purchase order on a sole source basis to Addium, Inc (1300 NE Henley Court, Ste. 6, Pullman WA 99163-56662) for the procurement of (1) Aqualab VSA Vapor Sorption Analyzer Part #40430; (1) VSA Service Training Part #50194; (1) Aqualab WVTR Testing Kit Part #40237; (1) Moisture Analysis Toolkit 3.0 Part #50229; (1) Aqualab Stainless Steel Cups Part #40314; and shipping if applicable. Statutory Authority This purchase is being conducted under the authority of FAR 12. The FSIS has determined that Addium, Inc. is the only source reasonably available to satisfy this requirement of the Aqualab VSA Vapor Sorption Analyzer from Addium, Inc. because of their unique capabilities exclusive to their product. The Aqualab VSA can perform dynamic dewpoint isotherms, which is proprietary. Unlike the conventional dynamic vapor sorption isotherm method, dynamic dewpoint isotherms are independent of sample equilibration for setting water activities, allowing for increased precision and detection of inflection points in isotherm curves indicative of critical relative humidities. This would allow us to determine appropriate storage conditions that do not lead to migration of components and deterioration in product quality, such as with sugar blooming. Since this is a proprietary method, no other vapor sorption analyzer on the market has these capabilities. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. It�s a synopsis for informational purposes only. However, any responsible source that believes it can meet this requirement may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. Responses must include: 1. Company Name and CAGE Code. 2. Technical description of how the proposed alternative meets all requirements listed above. Responses will be used to determine if a competitive procurement is necessary, at the discretion of the Contracting Officer.

title: Cyber Platform
description: The Government seeks a commercially available Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) cybersecurity training platform that provides immersive, hands-on cyber learning, realistic cyber laboratory environments, structured learning pathways, cyber range exercises, and cybersecurity certification preparation capabilities that enhance cyber workforce readiness, operational problem-solving, critical thinking, and cyber mission effectiveness.
